newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds nudge up on foreign investor interest.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds nudge up on foreign investor interest.

text.p: Danish bond prices nudged up in a positive market with solid foreign investor interest on Wednesday and dealers said they were broadly optimistic about the government's economic plan to be launched in the early afternoon.
"People are reasonably hopeful about any government plan to reduce state debt and shore up the economic upturn. Only good come come of it," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.06 point from the pre-market at 109.88, yielding 6.49 percent in turnover of 1.9 billion crowns.
The benchmark 2006's June future rose 0.40 point to 109.34 with 67 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.15 point to 88.15.
The crown traded at 3.8072 per mark at 1050 gmt, up a smidgen from around 3.8075 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed one basis point to 69.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling around one billion crowns worth of various bond series as part of its routine financing operations.
